claims.explanation: Dofetilide is a potent blocker of the hERG (KCNH2) potassium channel, and its selective killing likely reflects dependence of sensitive cancer lines on hERG/KCNH2 activity for proliferation or survival, with additional contribution from other potassium channels such as KCNH1, KCNJ12, and KCNK2. Lines with high expression of these channels or with mutations that create ionic dependencies (e.g., TP53, PTEN, BRAF, EGFR, KRAS pathway alterations) may be more vulnerable, while lines with low channel expression or alternative survival signaling are protected.

features.basis: Dofetilide is a high-affinity hERG/KCNH2 blocker; hERG expression is required for drug sensitivity
Annotated dofetilide target; EAG1 potassium channel can support proliferation
Annotated dofetilide target; inward rectifier may contribute to membrane potential control
Annotated dofetilide target; two-pore potassium channel affects excitability and survival
TP53 mutations are enriched in many selectively killed lines, suggesting loss of p53-mediated survival checkpoints
PTEN loss appears in several sensitive lines and may increase dependence on potassium channel-linked survival signals
BRAF mutations are present in multiple sensitive melanoma and colorectal lines
EGFR mutations appear in sensitive lung and glioma lines, possibly linking RTK signaling to ion channel dependence
KRAS mutations are common in sensitive pancreatic and colorectal lines
ARID1A mutations appear in both sensitive and resistant lines, but several least-affected lines carry ARID1A mutations, suggesting possible resistance association
SMARCA4 mutations are present in several least-affected lines, suggesting chromatin remodeling loss may reduce drug sensitivity
NF1 mutations appear in multiple least-affected lines, possibly indicating alternative survival pathways
